title: local-ensemble-orchestrator-proto-scratchpad
content:
Context and intent:
This is a personal scratchpad for a lightweight local ensemble orchestrator that can run inside the client-side proxy or a small edge sidecar. Goal: enable apps to compose multiple small/fast model variants and heuristics to produce higher-quality responses with predictable cost and local latency bounds.

Goals / non-goals:
- Goal: define simple API + runtime semantics for (1) orchestrating N local models, (2) merging/stitching outputs, (3) providing deterministic replayability and introspectable telemetry.
- Goal: support hybrid fallback to remote Redwood hosted models when local ensemble can't satisfy constraints (quality/latency/cost).
- Non-goal: building full ensemble-training logic or heavy-weight aggregators — this is runtime composition only.

High-level runtime pieces:
- Agent: the process that accepts a request and drives ensemble execution. Runs in-proc (client lib) or as a sidecar.
- Model adapters: thin shims to local models (ONNX, GGML, quantized llama variants, tiny-cpu models) exposing uniform interface: async generate(token_streaming=false, max_tokens, stop).
- Router: policy engine that picks which adapters to run and in what mode (speculative, parallel, cascade).
- Merger: deterministic merge policy for multiple completions (voting, pick-score, stitch-by-span).
- Telemetry tap: samples candidate outputs, logs divergence metrics, cost estimate, latency.
- Fallback bridge: circuit to Redwood cloud endpoint when local run fails SLO or triggers privacy rule.

API shape sketch (proto / JSON-over-HTTP style):
- POST /v1/local-ensemble/generate
  Request body (JSON):
  {
    "input": "string",
    "session_id": "string (opt)",
    "ensemble_policy": "string | inline-policy",
    "max_tokens": 256,
    "modes": {
      "speculative_parallel": true,
      "cascade_threshold_ms": 120
    },
    "telemetry": {"sample_rate": 0.02}
  }

  Response (streamed chunks or final JSON):
  {
    "response": "final text",
    "provenance": ["model-a:v1","model-b:v2"],
    "merge_strategy": "voting",
    "trace_id": "uuid",
    "metrics": {"latency_ms": 72, "tokens_local": 54, "tokens_remote": 0}
  }

Policy DSL examples (informal):
- minimal: "fast": prefer smallest model, allow speculative run of medium model if confidence<0.6
- balanced: "cost-aware": run small model; if low-confidence and latency budget allows, run medium in parallel and merge; if both disagree, call remote-hosted fallback with pinning to model X.

Speculative/parallel semantics notes:
- Speculative parallel: start with fast model (M1) streaming result; concurrently start M2 (higher quality) but only if runtime CPU/GPU budget indicates OK. Merger must be able to reconcile partial streams — prefer earliest complete higher-confidence span.
- Cascade: run smallest model first; if confidence < threshold after full completion, run larger model. This saves cost but adds latency.

Merge policies (deterministic):
1) Majority-vote at sentence-span granularity.
2) Confidence-weighted pick (weights come from model calibrator or light scorer).
3) Stitch-by-span: take M1 for first N tokens, if M2 diverges on a later sentence and passes quality check, splice and label with provenance.
4) Fallback-to-remote if merge ambiguity > X or safety check fails.

Caching / KV sharing idea:
- Shared prefix KV: if M1 computes KV cache for first tokens, allow M2 to warm its cache off M1’s prefix when compatible architecture. Keep small shared cache with eviction TTL keyed by session_id+prompt-hash.

Session and replay semantics:
- Each generate gets a trace_id and deterministic seed. The orchestrator should record: input, chosen adapters + versions, merge decisions, sampled telemetry. This enables exact replay (given adapters are deterministic or seeded).
- For privacy, allow "ephemeral" mode where only aggregates (latency, success/fail) are stored and raw prompt is not persisted.

Operational signals and metrics to emit:
- per-request: orchestrator_latency_ms, models_invoked[], tokens_local, tokens_remote, merge_strategy, merge_confidence_score
- per-model: avg_latency, avg_confidence, error_rate, memory_pressure
- alarms: consecutive_local_failures -> escalate to remote fallback; memory_pressure high -> drop speculative runs

Failure modes and mitigations:
- Model crash during parallel run -> ignore crash and continue with survivors; emit error and optionally trigger rollback to last-known-safe model set.
- Non-deterministic outputs -> record seed and calibrate models; consider adding small deterministic re-ranking scorer to make merging stable.
- Resource exhaustion -> switch to strict cascade (no parallelism) and reduced max_tokens.

Privacy and security considerations:
- Local-only mode: forbid remote fallback; useful for strict data residency. Enforce in policy.
- Telemetry sampling should be opt-in per deployment; avoid storing PII. Allow in-line sanitizer hooks.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to encode "confidence" uniformly across heterogeneous models? (logit-avg, next-token entropy, separate scorer?)
- Merger complexity vs. developer UX: do we expose a library hook for custom merge functions or only DSL?
- How to estimate cost for mixed runs (CPU cost + potential remote cost) to feed routing decisions?
- Repro playbook for non-deterministic GPU kernels (quantized kernels may be non-deterministic). Need guidance.

Prototype next steps:
1) mock adapter for ggml/tiny on CPU + lightweight scorer process.
2) implement router with two policies: speculative_parallel and cascade.
3) basic merger: majority-vote by sentence with provenance labels.
4) add simple fallback path to Redwood hosted API and circuit breaker.

Rough interface snippet (pseudo-JS):
const resp = await ensemble.generate({
  input: "Summarize the invoice",
  policy: "cost-aware",
  session: "s-123",
  maxTokens: 200
});
// resp: { text, provenance: ['tiny-cpu:v0','med-gpu-q4:v2'], merge: 'voting' }

Notes-to-self:
- Keep API small and opinionated. Start with 2 policies. Avoid exposing full scheduling DSL initially.
- Add a reproducible test harness that runs N seeds and asserts merger stability.

End of scratchpad.
